idea: A worn pad printed with Muybridge's running horse lies still on a desk until its pages start to riffle, the horse gallops, and the pad slows and stops on the first frame of the stride.
leave: Twenty still photographs are enough to make a horse run.
subject: the horse printed on the pages, from still picture to gallop and back

device.what: a real flip book, filmed from above, whose pages turn faster and then slower
device.why: the horse only moves while the pages turn, so the speed of the riffle is the speed of the story

change.from: a small pad on a brown desk, a photograph of a horse and rider on its top page
change.to: the first pages lifting over the spine as the view moves in close

change.from: close on the right-hand page, a page in mid-turn
change.to: after pages flying past ten a second with the horse galloping, the riffle slowing, a page still in the air

change.from: close on the pad, a page turning slowly
change.to: the whole pad at rest on the desk, the horse back on its first frame, flipbook written below
